Evaluate energy use and emissions of H production pathways to injection point: ANL 2 will evaluate the impacts of primary energy sources and technology pathways of H on total 2 and fossil energy use and GHG and CAP emissions. The technology pathways will include renewable and near-zero-carbon H production via low-temperature electrolysis and high- 2 temperature electrolysis using solar, wind, and nuclear power. The evaluation will also include H compression technologies for various storage types, including geologic and 2 physical storage options, as well as compression for various H pipeline transportation 2 distances to the injection point, which will be informed by TEA and regional analysis conducted by NREL. 2. Evaluate energy and emissions of delivering H /NG blends from injection point to end-use 2 applications: ANL will evaluate the impacts of the combustion of various H /NG blend ratios on the 2 efficiency and emissions of existing internal combustion engines driving the pipeline compressors. Such evaluation will leverage the most recent experiments at ANL and will benefit from a thorough literature review of using H /NG blends in internal combustion engines. ANL will also evaluate the 2 implications of leakage and fugitive emissions of H /NG gas blends in lieu of CH leakage associated 2 4 with conventional gas pathways. While CH leakage is a major contribution to life cycle GHG 4 emissions for conventional NG pathways due to its high global warming potential (30), H leakage 2 could be of greater magnitude due to it being a smaller molecule and would represent energy and economic loss, in addition to its impact on changing the blending ratio along the pathway of the blend to end use. Finally, ANL will evaluate the energy and environmental implications of pipeline modification, materials, and construction to accommodate various blending ratios in lieu of a counterfactual scenario where H is delivered in a newly dedicated pipeline to various end uses. 2 18 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. 3. Evaluate emissions of H /NG combustion at various end-use applications: ANL will 2 evaluate the life cycle impacts of H /NG combustion at various end-use applications, 2 including building appliances, turbines, engines, and industrial boilers and heating applications. The evaluation will span varying blending ratios because it impacts both flame temperature and combustion characteristics, with consequent impacts on energy efficiency and emissions. In particular, NO emissions are strongly impacted by combustion x temperature, and its mitigation may have a negative impact on energy efficiency at end use. 4.
